title: Black Pepper Soy Curls
subtitle: with sticky rice
menu_blurb: Protein-rich soy curls stir-fried with peppers, onion, broccoli, garlic and ginger in a bold black pepper sauce, inspired by classic Sichuan chicken.
intro: Delicious flavor with colorful veggies, and it’s vegan! Super easy, too. Soy curls are a great staple for vegetarians and vegans because they are protein-based and so versatile: spice them up or marinate them, bake them, pan fry them, shred them, crisp them.
origin: Inspired by Sichuan pepper chicken. Szechuan chicken comes from Sichuan province in southwestern China, a region renowned for its bold, spicy, aromatic cuisine. It is defined by “mala” flavor, a combination of numbing Sichuan peppercorns and spicy chili peppers. Authentic versions stir-fry crispy chicken with dried chilies and peppercorns.

mise_en_place.task: Soy curls in water for 10 minutes, then marinate them in broth

mise_en_place.label: Blanch
mise_en_place.task: Broccoli in boiling water for 4 minutes, then drain into ice water

mise_en_place.label: Chop
mise_en_place.task: Peppers, onions, broccoli, garlic, and ginger

mise_en_place.label: Assemble
mise_en_place.task: All of the sauces and spices

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: A knife, a rice cooker, and a bowl of ice water for blanching

ingredients.note: Plant-based swap: use a vegetarian (mushroom) oyster sauce.

items.name: Green and red bell peppers, chopped medium

steps.title: Make the rice
instructions: Add 2 cups of rice to the rice cooker and rinse until the water is no longer cloudy. Add water up to the first line of your pointer finger ☺

steps.title: Soak the soy curls
instructions: Warm the broth in a medium bowl in the microwave, add the soy curls, and soak for 15 minutes.
Drain, reserving the soaking liquid, and press lightly to remove excess moisture. Transfer to a bowl.

steps.title: Crisp the soy curls
instructions: In a small bowl, mix the garlic powder, black pepper, and rice flour.
Toss the soy curls with the soy sauce, then coat them with the rice flour mixture.
Pan fry in a skillet over medium heat with a generous coat of cooking spray and 1 teaspoon of oil, crisping each side for 3 to 4 minutes. Move to a separate bowl.
Meanwhile, mix all of the sauce ingredients in a bowl and set aside.

steps.title: Sauté the vegetables
instructions: Once the soy curls are done, heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and add the oil.
When the oil is hot, add the onions and peppers. Once half cooked, add the garlic and ginger, then the broccoli and a pinch of salt. Toss well.
Cook for a minute or two. The vegetables should stay crunchy, and the garlic should just start to turn golden.

steps.title: Bring it together
instructions: As soon as the garlic turns golden, add the sauce mixture. Bring to a boil and cook for about a minute, until the sauce thickens.
Add the crispy soy curls, toss well, and take off the heat.
Taste and adjust: a little more maple syrup for sweetness, more oyster sauce for depth, or more black pepper or red pepper flakes for heat.

steps.title: Serve
instructions: Spoon over a small bowl of rice or cooked grains, garnish with sesame seeds and peanuts, and enjoy!

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: The longer you marinate the soy curls, the tastier they will be.

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Try other vegetables, like water chestnuts, bamboo shoots, carrots, green beans, or Chinese eggplant. You can also swap the soy curls for seitan.

notebook.question: What are soy curls, and are they good for you?
answer: Yes! Soy curls are made from non-GMO whole soybeans, without chemical pesticides, preservatives, or additives. They are also a great source of protein, fiber, iron, and potassium.

notebook.question: What’s the difference between soy curls and tofu?
answer: Tofu is minimally processed but not a whole food. It provides high-quality protein, healthy fats, and often added calcium. Soy curls are closer to a whole food than most processed soy products, retaining the fiber and protein of whole soybeans, though some nutrients are lost in processing.
